text.p: The jury in O.J. Simpson's civil trial entered its third day of deliberations on Thursday to decide if the former football star was responsible for the deaths of his ex-wife and her friend.

The jury deliberated for a total of just over eight hours Tuesday and Wednesday, poring over photographic evidence with a magnifying glass and examining a test tube similar to the one used to store Simpson's blood sample taken by police the day after Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman were stabbed and slashed to death.

Simpson was acquitted of the June 12, 1994, murders by a criminal court jury in October 1995. He is now battling a wrongful death lawsuit brought by the families of the victims, who are seeking substantial damages.
Should the panel find Simpson liable for the murders, they must also assess compensatory damages before announcing their verdict.
In the event of a verdict against Simpson, a second phase of the trial will follow in which the jury will be asked to decide how much he must pay in punitive damages.
